title: A PR review run is gated only by enrolment, so any stranger's PR spends money
description:
Raised by tick v7g, which correctly declined to decide it alone.

Enrolment of a repository is currently the ONLY gate on a PR review run. So every incoming pull request against an enrolled repo starts a paid run. On a public repository that is an open door: anyone can open pull requests, and each one costs money, with no human between the stranger and the spend.

Compare what Phase 3 did for the sibling case. An ISSUE needs the tk consent label before it becomes even a draft, and a draft needs a human press before anything runs. A PULL REQUEST currently needs neither — it goes straight to a run. The asymmetry is not defensible: a PR is more expensive to process than an issue, and equally stranger-authored.

This is the shape Phase 2's cost lessons and Phase 3's consent boundary both point at, so it should be settled before Phase 4 closes rather than carried.

Options to weigh, not a prescription:
- The same consent-label boundary as issues, applied to PRs.
- Author trust: members/collaborators reviewed automatically, outside contributors requiring a label or a human press.
- A per-repo daily review budget, so the worst case is bounded even if the gate is generous.
Whichever is chosen, the read-only grade already bounds the DAMAGE; what is unbounded today is the COST.

acceptance_criteria: A pull request from someone with no write access to an enrolled repo cannot start a paid run without either a consent signal or a human press; the chosen rule is documented and pinned by tests, including the outside-contributor case.
closed_reason: Completed: a PR review run is gated on the author having write access to the base repository, with a consent label as the escape hatch for outside contributors and a per-repo daily review budget as the backstop for the gate being wrong. Closes the asymmetry where an issue needed a consent label and a human press while a pull request — costlier and equally stranger-authored — needed only enrolment. The read-only grade already bounded the damage; this bounds the cost.
